correctness.rationale: Compact isometry groups admit a common invariant Euclidean inner product, placing the Lie algebra in so(5). Simultaneous diagonalization bounds commuting skew-symmetric directions at two. A compact real Lie algebra of dimension five is either abelian or su(2) plus a two-dimensional center (compact semisimple factors have dimensions 3 or at least 8); either contains at least three commuting directions, a contradiction. The directly inspected Theorem 3(a) of Rosenthal (1986) forces dimensions strictly above six to equal ten. Connected-component preservation of extreme-point Euclidean block spheres proves the full identity isometry group of each listed ell-one sum is exactly the product of SO(d_j), not merely a subgroup; all seven dimensions are thereby attained. Assumptions are real, finite and exactly 5D. No infinite claim rests on sampling.

value.rationale: The natural exact invariant \(\dim\mathcal Z(X)\) measures continuous isometric symmetry and is central to numerical index zero and operator geometry. The complete ambient-dimension-five range was expressly posed as an unanswered research problem in Kadets--Martín--Payá (2006, Problem 28) and reiterated in Martín (2009, Problem 1.3.7). The result removes the only low-range uncertainty and supplies explicit models for each remaining value; it is a motivated complete classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or known table recomputation. The scope is the dimension spectrum, not full norm classification.
